item.title: Aichi Events 2026: Nagoya Sumo, Fireworks, Tenno Festival & Ghibli Park
item.description: Aichi — with Nagoya at its heart — is the manufacturing engine of Japan, but its 2026 event calendar is pure summer spectacle and samurai heritage. The prefecture hosts a July Grand Sumo tournament in a brand-new arena, some of the country’s biggest fireworks in its “Mikawa fireworks” heartland, a 600-year-old UNESCO river festival, a procession of the three warlords who unified Japan, and Studio Ghibli’s own theme park. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Akita Events 2026: Kanto Festival, Omagari Fireworks & Namahage
item.description: Akita’s calendar swings between two extremes: a summer of luminous festivals and Japan’s most prestigious fireworks, and a deep winter of snow igloos and demon rituals. The Kanto Festival’s forests of balanced lantern-poles are one of Tohoku’s three great summer festivals; the Omagari competition is where Japan’s top pyrotechnicians battle for the national crown; and in February, the Oga Peninsula’s Namahage demons and Yokote’s candle-lit snow huts define northern winter. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Fukuoka Events 2026: Yamakasa, Dontaku, Kanmon Fireworks & Kyushu Sumo
item.description: Fukuoka wears its festival culture on its sleeve. Hakata — the old merchant heart of the city — hosts two of Kyushu’s most explosive festivals within months of each other (Dontaku in May, Yamakasa in July), the region’s only Grand Sumo tournament arrives each November, and one of Japan’s biggest fireworks displays lights up the Kanmon Strait in August. Add a week-long autumn shrine festival famous for its food stalls, and Fukuoka’s 2026 calendar rewards a well-timed trip.

item.title: Gifu Events 2026: Takayama Festival, Gujo Odori & Cormorant Fishing
item.description: Gifu’s mountainous heart hosts some of Japan’s most refined and enduring traditions. The Takayama Festival’s ornate automaton floats are counted among the country’s most beautiful; Gujo Odori is a dance the whole town joins for two months, culminating in four all-night sessions; and on the Nagara River, cormorant fishing has continued unbroken for 1,300 years. Add the winter magic of Shirakawa-go’s illuminated thatched village, and Gifu rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Kagawa Events 2026: Takamatsu Festival Fireworks, Konpira & Art Islands
item.description: Kagawa, Japan’s smallest prefecture, punches far above its size — home of Sanuki udon, the pilgrimage shrine of Konpira-san, the celebrated Ritsurin Garden, and the “art islands” of the Seto Inland Sea. Its 2026 event calendar centres on a lively summer festival with fireworks over Takamatsu’s harbour, alongside year-round island art and one of Japan’s finest strolling gardens. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Kagoshima Events 2026: Kinko Bay Fireworks, Ohara Matsuri & Sakurajima
item.description: Kagoshima lives in the shadow of Sakurajima, one of the world’s most active volcanoes, which smokes across the bay from the city every day. Its 2026 event calendar matches that drama: Kyushu’s largest fireworks display over Kinko Bay, southern Japan’s biggest street dance festival, and the year-round spectacle of the volcano itself. Add the steaming sand baths of Ibusuki and the ancient forests of Yakushima offshore, and Kagoshima rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Kanagawa Events 2026: Yokohama Fireworks, Tanabata & Hakone Parade
item.description: Kanagawa packs an unusual variety into one prefecture: the harbour glamour of Yokohama, the temples and beaches of Kamakura and Shonan, and the mountain onsen of Hakone. Its 2026 event calendar is just as varied — near-monthly fireworks over Yokohama’s port, one of the Kanto region’s three great Tanabata festivals, a feudal-lord procession through Hakone, and horseback archery at Kamakura’s great shrine. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Mie Events 2026: Ise Fireworks, Kumano Fireworks & Ueno Tenjin
item.description: Mie is the spiritual heart of Japan — home to Ise Jingu, the most sacred of all Shinto shrines — and its 2026 event calendar blends the sacred with the spectacular. Two of the country’s finest fireworks displays light up the Ise river and the Kumano sea within a month of each other; a ninja-country festival parades through Iga; and one of Japan’s largest winter illuminations glows at Nabana no Sato.

item.title: Nagano Events 2026: Nozawa Fire Festival, Suwa Fireworks & Snow Monkeys
item.description: Nagano’s events run with its mountains and seasons: a fiery midwinter ritual in a snowbound onsen village, one of Japan’s largest fireworks displays over a mountain lake, the famous macaques bathing in steaming pools, and cherry blossoms so celebrated they draw crowds to a former castle in the hills. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end. A note on dates: Confirmed 2026 dates are given where announced.

item.title: Nagasaki Events 2026: Lantern Festival, Kunchi & Shoro Nagashi
item.description: Nagasaki’s centuries as Japan’s window to China and the West shaped an event calendar unlike anywhere else in the country. The Lantern Festival fills the city with 15,000 Chinese lanterns each February; the Kunchi festival blends Japanese, Chinese, and Dutch influences into a spectacular autumn procession; and the deeply moving August 9 Peace Ceremony and the firecracker-lit Shoro Nagashi spirit boats give the summer a solemn power. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Oita Events 2026: Beppu Fireworks, Onsen Festival & Usuki Takeyoi
item.description: Oita is Japan’s onsen capital — Beppu and Yufuin between them pour out more hot-spring water than anywhere else in the country — and its 2026 event calendar reflects that steamy character. A spring festival celebrates the hot springs themselves, summer brings fireworks over Beppu Bay, and autumn glows with thousands of bamboo lanterns in a castle town. Add the ever-bubbling “hells” of Beppu, and Oita rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Okayama Events 2026: Saidaiji Naked Festival, Momotaro & Korakuen
item.description: Okayama — the sunny “Land of Sunshine” on the Seto Inland Sea — mixes one of Japan’s wildest winter rituals with the serene beauty of a great garden. In February, thousands of men in loincloths battle for lucky sticks in near-darkness at Saidaiji; in summer, a festival named for the folk hero Momotaro fills the city with dance and fireworks; and year-round, the celebrated Korakuen garden glows with seasonal illuminations. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Saga Events 2026: Balloon Fiesta, Karatsu Kunchi & Arita Ceramics Fair
item.description: Saga packs a remarkable run of events into a single autumn week — Asia’s largest hot-air balloon competition fills the sky over the Kase River just as one of Japan’s most spectacular float festivals rolls through nearby Karatsu. Add Japan’s most famous ceramics fair each Golden Week and the porcelain heritage of Arita and Imari, and this quiet Kyushu prefecture rewards a well-timed 2026 trip. This guide gathers the events worth planning around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Shiga Events 2026: Biwako Fireworks, Otsu Matsuri & Sagicho
item.description: Shiga wraps around Lake Biwa, Japan’s largest lake, and its 2026 event calendar plays out on and around the water: one of the Kansai region’s biggest fireworks displays over the lake in Otsu, a rare simultaneous show fired from three shores, and a set of centuries-old festivals in the historic towns that ring it. Add spring blossoms over the water and autumn colour at ancient temples, and Shiga rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Shizuoka Events 2026: Hamamatsu Kites, Fukuroi Fireworks & Mt Fuji
item.description: Shizuoka stretches from the slopes of Mt Fuji to the beaches of the Izu Peninsula, and its 2026 event calendar is as varied as its geography: giant kites battling over Hamamatsu’s dunes in spring, one of Japan’s premier fireworks competitions in summer, marine fireworks over Atami Bay across much of the year, and Japan’s earliest cherry blossoms on the Izu coast. Add the climbing season on Fuji itself, and Shizuoka rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Tokushima Events 2026: Awa Odori, Fireworks & Machi Asobi
item.description: Tokushima’s event calendar is defined by one of the most electrifying festivals on earth. For four August nights, the whole city of Tokushima becomes a stage for the Awa Odori — 400 years of dance, drums, and the cry of “fools dancing, fools watching, so dance!” Around it, the prefecture offers the roaring Naruto whirlpools at their spring peak, a twice-yearly anime festival that takes over the city, and the deep-mountain quiet of the Iya Valley.

item.title: Tokyo Events 2026: Festivals, Fireworks & One-Off Happenings
item.description: Tokyo runs on a calendar of its own. In any given month, the city is hosting a centuries-old shrine festival, a national sumo tournament, a fireworks display drawing a million spectators, a pop-culture collaboration that exists only in 2026, and a seasonal spectacle timed to the blossoms or the autumn leaves. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around — the fixed annual traditions, the summer fireworks, and the one-off happenings you can only catch this year — with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Hiroshima Events 2026: Peace Ceremony, Flower Festival, Kangensai & Fireworks
item.description: Hiroshima’s event calendar is unusually wide in tone. The August 6 Peace Memorial Ceremony is one of the world’s most significant annual commemorations; the Kangensai boat festival on Miyajima is one of Japan’s oldest and most atmospheric Shinto rituals; the Flower Festival draws over a million people during Golden Week. Add summer fireworks over the bay, a legendary sake festival, and a beloved baseball team, and Hiroshima rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Chiba Events 2026: Fireworks, Tokyo Game Show, Gion Festivals & Disney
item.description: Chiba is where most visitors land (Narita Airport) and where Tokyo Disney Resort actually sits — but the prefecture’s own 2026 event calendar is far richer than a transit stop suggests. It hosts some of the Kanto region’s biggest summer fireworks, two UNESCO-linked Gion float festivals on the same weekend, the world’s largest video-game show, a temple-steps display of thirty thousand hina dolls, and whale-and-dolphin watching off its Pacific coast. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Nara Events & Festivals 2026: Lanterns, Deer Ceremonies & Ancient Rituals
item.description: Nara’s festival calendar is one of the richest in Japan — not because it has manufactured tourist events, but because many of the ceremonies here are among the oldest continuously observed religious rituals in the world. The Omizutori water-drawing ceremony at Todai-ji has been performed every year since 752 AD without interruption. The Kasuga Taisha Mantoro lantern festival lights the same 3,000 lanterns that have been donated across 1,000 years. The annual deer antler cutting is a direct continuation of the tradition that has protected both deer and people since the 8th century.

item.title: Saitama Events 2026: Chichibu Night Festival, Kawagoe Matsuri & Fireworks
item.description: Just north of Tokyo, Saitama is an easy day trip that hides two of Japan’s most important festivals. The Chichibu Night Festival and the Kawagoe Matsuri are both UNESCO-recognised float processions, and the prefecture also stages a Guinness-record firework, a hillside of half a million moss-phlox blooms, and the “Little Edo” charm of Kawagoe’s warehouse district. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Hokkaido Events 2026: Snow Festival, Yosakoi Soran, Lavender & Fireworks
item.description: Hokkaido’s events follow its dramatic seasons. Winter brings the snow-and-ice spectacle the island is world-famous for — the Sapporo Snow Festival and a string of candle-lit and ice-carved events across the region. Then summer flips the script entirely: energetic street dancing in June, lavender fields and hillside fireworks in July, and one of Japan’s great food festivals in autumn. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Osaka Events 2026: Festivals, Fireworks, Sumo & USJ Happenings
item.description: Osaka does festivals the way it does everything — loud, warm, and food-first. The city’s 2026 calendar runs from one of Japan’s three great festivals (Tenjin Matsuri, with its river-boat procession and fireworks) to the heart-stopping cart races of Kishiwada Danjiri, a spring Grand Sumo tournament, the year’s biggest anime collaborations at Universal Studios Japan, and a cherry-blossom tunnel opened for just one week. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Kyoto Events 2026: Gion Matsuri, the Three Great Festivals & Seasonal Light-Ups
item.description: No city in Japan keeps its festival calendar the way Kyoto does. The former capital hosts three of the country’s most storied processions — Aoi, Gion, and Jidai — each a living re-enactment of the imperial and medieval past, alongside a mountainside bonfire seen for miles, a torch-lit fire festival in the northern hills, private geisha dances, and seasonal temple light-ups timed to the cherry blossoms and autumn maples. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Best Time to Visit Japan for Cherry Blossoms 2026
item.description: Best Time to Visit Japan for Cherry Blossoms 2026: The Complete Seasonal Guide Spring in Japan isn’t just a season — it’s a collective exhale. After months of grey winter skies, the entire country erupts in waves of pale pink, and life shifts outdoors. If you’re planning a trip and searching for the best time to visit Japan for cherry blossoms 2026, you’ve come to the right place. I’ve lived here for fifteen years, and I still catch my breath every single spring.

item.title: Japan Autumn Leaves 2026: Peak Times & Best Spots by Region
item.description: Japan Autumn Leaves 2026 Peak Times by Region: The Complete Insider Guide to Kōyō Season There is no more breathtaking time to visit Japan than autumn. From late September through early December, the archipelago transforms into a rolling canvas of crimson, amber, and gold — a phenomenon the Japanese call kōyō (紅葉). If you’re planning a trip and searching for Japan autumn leaves 2026 peak times by region, you’ve come to the right place.

item.title: Japan Golden Week 2026: Travel Tips and Crowds to Avoid
item.description: Japan Golden Week 2026 Travel Tips: Should You Avoid It or Embrace the Chaos? Every spring, Japan enters one of its most electric — and most polarizing — travel periods. Golden Week, the cluster of national holidays running from late April to early May, sends roughly 70 million domestic travelers surging across the country. If you’re planning a spring trip and Googling “Japan Golden Week 2026 travel tips should you avoid,” you’re asking exactly the right question.

item.title: Japan Summer Festivals 2026 Matsuri Schedule by Region
item.description: Japan Summer Festivals 2026: The Ultimate Matsuri Schedule by Region There is no season that captures the soul of Japan quite like summer. From late June through August, the entire country erupts in a kaleidoscope of lantern-lit processions, thundering taiko drums, explosive fireworks, and centuries-old dances that transform quiet neighborhoods into raucous celebrations. If you’re planning a trip around Japan summer festivals 2026 matsuri schedule by region, you’re making one of the best decisions of your traveling life — and this guide will help you make the most of every sweaty, exhilarating, deeply delicious moment.

item.title: Japan Summer Festivals 2026 Matsuri Schedule Guide
item.description: Japan Summer Festivals 2026: The Ultimate Matsuri Schedule, Dates & Insider Guide There is no better time to witness Japan at its most electrifying than during the summer months, when the entire country erupts in a blaze of fireworks, thundering taiko drums, and thousands of dancers weaving through lantern-lit streets. If you’re planning a trip around the Japan summer festivals 2026 matsuri schedule dates, you’re in for something truly extraordinary — a season that reveals a side of Japan that no amount of temple-hopping or bullet-train-riding can match.

item.title: Kyoto Cherry Blossom 2026 Spring Guide Best Spots
item.description: Kyoto Cherry Blossom 2026: Best Spots, Dates, Forecast & Complete Seasonal Guide Meta Description Plan your Kyoto cherry blossom 2026 trip with our insider guide to the best spots, dates, forecast, seasonal food, and local tips from a 15-year Japan resident. Introduction: Why Kyoto in Cherry Blossom Season Is Unlike Anywhere Else on Earth There are a handful of travel experiences that genuinely change how you see the world. Standing beneath a cascade of pale pink petals at a 400-year-old Kyoto temple at dawn — the air cool, the light golden, the silence broken only by birdsong and the whisper of falling blossoms — is one of them.

item.title: Spring 2026 Kyoto Cherry Blossom Forecast and Best Spots
item.description: Kyoto Cherry Blossom 2026 Forecast: Best Spots, Peak Dates & Insider Tips for an Unforgettable Spring Spring in Kyoto isn’t just a season — it’s a kind of collective exhale that an entire city has been waiting for. After months of grey skies and biting winds whipping through the narrow machiya-lined streets, the first pale-pink buds crack open and everything changes. The light softens. The rivers turn pastel. Strangers share blankets and sake under centuries-old trees.
